name: Microsoft Azure ND A100 v4 (ND96asr 40GB and ND96amsr 80GB)
price_basis: per A100 GPU-hour. ND96amsr A100 v4 = 8x A100 80GB, Linux on-demand $32.77/instance-hr / 8 = $4.096; Spot $8.441552 = $1.0552; Low Priority $6.554 = $0.8193. ND96asr A100 v4 = 8x A100 40GB, on-demand $31.613 or $27.197 depending on meter (_NU vs plain); Spot $5.904469. Fetched from the Retail Prices API 2026-10-03.
notes: Genuinely available where the H100/H200 SKUs are not, and the spot rate is remarkable: $1.06 per A100-hour on 80GB parts, an ~74% discount, which is within a whisker of AWS's Capacity Block p4d rate ($1.475) and of Oracle's on-demand A100 80GB ($4.00 is on-demand; the spot is the steal here). Low Priority at $0.82/A100-hour is cheaper still but is Batch-only and 30-minute max, so it is not a route to a serving endpoint. Watch the same API-multi-meter trap as the H100 record: the 40GB SKU returns $31.613 and $27.197 depending on which meter you read, so quote from the specific armSkuName you will actually launch. Azure A100 v4 does publish proper Reservation meters ($183,722/h and $378,926/h normalised), unlike the H100 v5 SKU, so a real reservation discount is on offer here. Hardware: dedicated 200 Gb/s Mellanox HDR InfiniBand per GPU, 1.6 Tb/s per VM.
